stem:
Ravi looked at a drop of pond water under a microscope in his school laboratory in Patna. He saw a tiny Amoeba moving about, feeding and reproducing, all on its own.
Ravi said, "It has only one cell, so it cannot be a complete living organism."
Which statement about the Amoeba is correct?

options.text: It is a complete living organism because one cell carries out all the functions needed for survival.
It is not a living organism because all living organisms are made of many cells.
It is alive only when it joins with other Amoeba cells to form a group.
It is a complete organism only because it lives in pond water.

teacher.key_rationale: An Amoeba is a unicellular organism; its single cell performs feeding, movement, respiration and reproduction, so it is a complete living organism. B denies life to all unicellular organisms, C invents a colony requirement, D makes habitat the criterion.
